answer: An orchard API serving violet ground-cover records can require one cipher puzzle per query. The server signs a fresh 128-bit nonce, query digest and expiry. A client searches AES keys until encrypting that nonce yields 20 leading zero bits; the server checks one encryption and consumes the nonce atomically. Fresh accounts cannot reuse solved stamps: each extra query needs fresh work, averaging 2^20 trials under ideal-cipher assumptions. Parallel hardware still buys more access.
